body: Delta-state CRDTs are a refinement of state-based CRDTs that ship only the changes — the delta-mutators — rather than the full state on every sync. Each delta is itself a join-semilattice element, so merging a delta into a replica is the same operation as merging full states. This keeps the convergence guarantees of CvRDTs while approaching the payload size of operation-based CRDTs. Ditto and Automerge both use this design.

Causal ordering between replicas requires a logical clock. A Lamport clock is a single integer per peer that ticks on every local event and on every received message; it gives a total order but loses concurrency information. A vector clock keeps one counter per peer and can detect concurrent updates exactly, at the cost of growing with the peer count.

A Hybrid Logical Clock (HLC) blends a Lamport clock with wall-clock time: each event gets a (physical, logical) pair where the physical part tracks wall time and the logical part breaks ties when events happen within the same millisecond. HLCs are bounded in size, give human-readable timestamps, and preserve causality. Ditto uses HLCs to tag every CRDT operation so peers can order updates without coordination.

Ditto models documents as nested CRDT Maps where each field is itself a CRDT (Register, Counter, Set, Map, or List). Sync over the mesh ships dot-tagged delta nodes rather than per-peer per-field deltas, so a document changed once syncs to everyone in O(change) bytes regardless of replica count. Combined with the BLE transport, this makes phone-to-phone document sync feasible without a server.

Sequence CRDTs — used for collaborative text editing — assign each character a dense, dynamically-allocated identifier so concurrent insertions at the same position get a well-defined order. RGA (Replicated Growable Array) and the Logoot/LSEQ families take different approaches: RGA uses an append-only tree with a deletion bit, while Logoot identifiers are variable-length fractional indices. Tombstones accumulate over time, which is why long-lived text documents need garbage collection.
